description: Multi-dimensional adversarial review of a diff or capability: correctness, security, and spec compliance, with every finding adversarially verified before it is reported.

findings.title: Sign-out reports every non-204/401 response, including a 403 CSRF rejection, as 'Could not reach the server.'
findings.evidence: `signOut()` throws `UnexpectedStatus` for any status other than 204/401 (session.ts:31). The contract lists 403 Forbidden for DELETE /api/admin/session, which happens when the XSRF-TOKEN cookie is missing or stale. The catch block in AdminHome sets `failed` and shows `t('admin.session.unreachable')` ('Could not reach the server.'). The server was reachable but refused the request, so the user gets a wrong diagnosis, and retrying keeps failing the same way. The sign-out button also has no busy/disabled state, so repeated clicks send concurrent DELETEs.
findings.suggestion: Tell transport failures (TypeError from fetch) apart from HTTP error statuses and show a separate 'Sign-out failed' message for the HTTP case. On 403, refetch the session or reload so a fresh XSRF token is issued. Disable the button while the request is in flight, the same way SignInForm uses `busy`.

findings.title: Sign-out and 401 expiry flip the session flag but leave other admin query data in the cache
findings.evidence: Both the 401 listener (`queryClient.setQueryData(ADMIN_SESSION_KEY, false)`) and AdminHome's sign-out only set `['admin','session']` to false. Every later admin slice will cache its data under `['admin', …]`. After sign-out or idle expiry (NFR-15), that data stays in memory, and after the next sign-in it can be shown stale without a refetch. No other admin queries exist yet, so nothing visible breaks today.
findings.suggestion: Put one `endAdminSession(queryClient)` helper in session.ts. It should call `queryClient.removeQueries({ queryKey: ['admin'] })` and then set ADMIN_SESSION_KEY to false. Use it from both the 401 listener and sign-out.

findings.title: Raw font-weight and rem width in feature CSS instead of design-system tokens or classes
findings.evidence: `.admin-label { font-weight: 700; }` and `.admin-stack { width: min(100%, 28rem); }` hardcode values. AGENTS.md says: 'For your own styles, use only its CSS variables … no raw hex, px or font values.' The design system already has `.dk-t-body-strong` (16px/700) and `.dk-t-label` for label text.
findings.suggestion: Remove `.admin-label` and give the <label> the `dk-t-body-strong` (or `dk-t-label`) class. Take the max width from an existing layout token, or derive it from spacing variables, rather than a raw `28rem`.

findings.title: Password field uses the child answer-input style (26px tabular numerals, 56px right padding)
findings.evidence: The input uses `className="dk-input"`. In components.css:131 that class is the task-answer input: `height: 60px; padding: 0 56px 0 …; font-size: 26px; font-weight: 600; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums`, and the 56px padding leaves room for a result icon. Reusing it for an admin password field gives an oversized answer-box look and reserves space for an icon that never appears.
findings.suggestion: Check src/design-system/README.md for a general text-input style or component for forms. If none exists, request one through the design-system artifact; don't repurpose the answer input.

findings.title: A second wrong password may not be re-announced to screen readers
findings.evidence:
After the first wrong password, `error` is 'invalid' and `

` stays mounted. Another wrong password calls `setError('invalid')` again with the same value, so React doesn't re-render the alert and its text doesn't change. Many screen readers announce a live region only when its content changes, so the second failure is silent apart from the field being cleared.
findings.suggestion: Clear `error` at the start of `submit` (`setError(null)` next to `setBusy(true)`), so the alert unmounts and remounts on every failed attempt, or key the alert by an attempt counter.

findings.title: Coverage summary: 7 scenarios: 6 implemented, 1 partial, 0 missing, 0 contradicted
findings.evidence: Checklist = the 4 delta scenarios (No session, Wrong password, Session ends while signed in, Sign-out CSRF) + the store admin-access scenarios with a UI or client half: 'Admin UI shows sign-in without a session', 'Idle timeout just past 8 hours … AND the admin UI shows the sign-in form', 'Reads need no CSRF token'. Implemented: No session (AdminGate.tsx:34, SignInForm.tsx:38-50, AdminArea.tsx:39; AdminGate.test.tsx:39, e2e/admin-sign-in.spec.ts:36). Session ends / idle expiry (adminClient.ts:37 + AdminGate.tsx:18; AdminGate.test.tsx:109). Sign-out CSRF (adminClient.ts:31; adminClient.test.ts:16, AdminGate.test.tsx:98, e2e:68). Reads without CSRF (adminClient.ts:5,31; adminClient.test.ts:23). Store 'shows sign-in without a session' (same as No session). Partial: Wrong password, because a repeated wrong attempt is not announced again (see the separate finding). All backend-only scenarios (cookie flags, 403 paths, password policy, LAN binding) are out of scope for this repo.
findings.suggestion: No action. This is the summary line the output contract asks for.

findings.title: Frontend traces and claims NFR-1 / NFR-15, but the capability plan assigns both to the backend only
findings.evidence: Plan ownership table (contract/docs/mvp-capability-plan.md:296,309): '| NFR-1 | admin-access | backend |', '| NFR-15 | admin-access | backend |'. AGENTS.md: 'Annotate with `// @trace FR-x` (only ids this repo owns)'. Code: AdminGate.test.tsx:1-2 '// @trace NFR-1 // @trace NFR-15', adminClient.test.ts:1 '// @trace NFR-15', e2e/admin-sign-in.spec.ts:1-2. proposal.md:7-8 says the change 'travels NFR-1 … NFR-15'. The plan's slice row (line 45) lists NFR-1/15/16 for the slice, and the §4.2 DoD (line 141) gives the frontend a sign-in route. So the plan contradicts itself, and the frontend has resolved it by claiming ownership without amending the plan.
findings.suggestion: Amend the docs store: change the Repo(s) column for NFR-1 and NFR-15 to 'backend, frontend', because the UI half (sign-in form, CSRF header, sign-in after a 401) is frontend-enforced. Then bump contract/. Otherwise, drop the @trace tags and trace only NFR-6/9/13.

findings.title: Repeated wrong password is not re-announced (scenario 'Wrong password' only partly met)
findings.evidence:
Delta scenario: 'WHEN the admin submits a password and sign-in answers 401 THEN "That password is not correct." is announced as an alert'. Code: setError('invalid') (line 26) leaves the state unchanged on a second wrong attempt, so the existing

stays mounted with the same text, and assistive tech does not announce it again. Tests (AdminGate.test.tsx:51, e2e:48) only cover the first attempt.
findings.suggestion: Clear the error before each submit (setError(null) at the start of submit()) or key the alert per attempt so it remounts. Add a unit test with two consecutive wrong passwords.

findings.title: Ticked task 3.1 names an artifact that does not exist (useAdminSession)
findings.evidence: Task: '- [x] 3.1 `src/features/admin-access/`: `adminClient`, `useAdminSession`, `AdminGate`, `SignInForm`, `AdminHome`.' No `useAdminSession` exists in the folder. Session logic lives in session.ts (checkAdminSession/signIn/signOut) and an inline useQuery in AdminGate.tsx:16. `AdminHome` is a private function inside AdminArea.tsx:10, not its own module.

findings.title: tasks.md checkboxes do not match current-state.md, and current-state.md is stale (says 'not committed')
findings.evidence: tasks.md:24 '- [ ] 4.5 Update `docs/current-state.md`' is unticked, but this branch did update current-state.md. That file says 'Active change: `implement-admin-access-ui` (slice 2, branch `slice2-admin-access`, not committed)', yet commit fa8a182 'feat(admin): admin sign-in screen and admin API client (slice 2)' exists on the branch.

findings.title: Undocumented UI states: checking, unreachable + retry, sign-in failure, sign-out failure
findings.evidence: The delta spec has only 'Admin sign-in screen' and 'CSRF header on admin mutations'. The code adds: a checking status (AdminGate.tsx:29), an unreachable alert with a 'Try again' button (lines 23-27), a non-401 sign-in failure message (SignInForm.tsx:29,51), and a sign-out failure alert (AdminArea.tsx:19-20,29). It also treats a sign-out 401 as success (session.ts:31). These appear in design.md and are unit-tested (AdminGate.test.tsx:122-171), but no Requirement/Scenario backs them.
findings.suggestion: Add a delta requirement such as 'Admin UI handles an unreachable backend' with scenarios for session-check failure + retry, sign-in 5xx versus 401, and a failed sign-out, so the behaviour is in the spec.

findings.title: Sign-out refused with 403 (missing/stale CSRF token) is shown as 'Could not reach the server.'
findings.evidence: Store spec 'Sign-out without a CSRF token is refused … HTTP 403'. adminClient.ts:31 sends no header when the XSRF-TOKEN cookie is missing (`&& token`). session.ts:31 throws on 403, and AdminArea shows t('admin.session.unreachable') = 'Could not reach the server.' (en.ts). The server was reached, so the copy is wrong and the admin cannot recover. The failure state also has no retry or re-sign-in path.
findings.suggestion: Map 403 on sign-out to its own message or to re-checking the session, and specify it in the delta spec (see the undocumented-states finding).

findings.title: Plan's NFR-9/NFR-13 DoD for the frontend (sign-in route in the a11y gate and ⟦ test) has no delta requirement
findings.evidence: mvp-capability-plan.md:141 'frontend: sign-in route in the a11y gate and the `⟦` render test.' It is implemented: route-paths.ts:5 ROUTE_PATHS = ['/', '/admin'] (iterated by the a11y/theme e2e), and i18n-coverage.test.tsx stubs the backend so /admin renders the sign-in form. proposal.md:9-10 cites NFR-9/NFR-13, but the delta spec has no requirement or scenario for them, so the slice's definition of done is not spec-backed.
findings.suggestion: Add a scenario to the delta spec: '/admin is in the route registry, passes axe in light and dark, and shows only catalog text under the ⟦ pseudo-catalog'.

findings.title: 'Any admin UI page' covers only the exact /admin route
findings.evidence: Store scenario: 'WHEN any admin UI page is opened THEN the English sign-in form … is shown instead of the page content'. Only '/admin' is registered. A path such as /admin/tasks falls to the not-found screen rather than the gate. No such page exists yet, so this is not a current violation, but nothing structurally guarantees later admin routes are wrapped in AdminGate.
findings.suggestion: When slice 5 adds admin routes, register them under AdminArea/AdminGate (or a /admin/* prefix rule). Consider a registry test that asserts every '/admin*' route is rendered inside AdminGate.

result.reasoning:
The finding holds up. In session.ts:29-31, `signOut()` throws `UnexpectedStatus` for any status other than 204 or 401, so a 403 throws. The adminClient middleware (adminClient.ts:34-39) only acts on 401 and passes 403 through, and nothing else catches it. In AdminArea.tsx:19-20, the bare `catch` sets `failed`, which shows `admin.session.unreachable`. en.ts:7 defines that string as 'Could not reach the server.' Network errors and HTTP-status errors land in the same catch, so a 403 from a server that answered is reported as unreachable.

The 403 case can actually happen:
- The generated schema lists 403 Forbidden on admin endpoints.
- The test backend (src/test/admin-backend.ts:45) returns 403 when X-XSRF-TOKEN is wrong.
- The client only attaches the header when the cookie exists (adminClient.ts:31). A missing cookie means no header, and the server rejects the request.

The Button at line 30 has no disabled or busy state, so repeated clicks send concurrent DELETEs. This side point is accurate but harmless, since sign-out is idempotent.

Severity stays minor. The only harm is a misleading message on a path that should be rare: the XSRF cookie is set at sign-in, so a 403 needs the cookie to be missing or stale.

I confirmed the mechanism in the code. `signOut()` (session.ts:29-32) throws `UnexpectedStatus` for any status other than 204/401. `AdminHome.handleSignOut` (AdminArea.tsx:15-22) catches everything with a bare `catch` and shows `admin.session.unreachable`, which en.ts:7 defines as "Could not reach the server." The contract (openapi.yaml:326-337, 1069-1075) lists 403 for DELETE /api/admin/session when the session is valid but the CSRF token is missing or wrong. So a server that is reachable and refuses the request gets misreported. A 5xx response gets the same wrong message.

The 403 can happen, but less often than the finding suggests:
- `xsrfToken()` reads the cookie on every request, so a token rotated in another tab is still picked up.
- A server restart that loses the session returns 401, which counts as success, not 403.
- A 403 needs the XSRF-TOKEN cookie to be cleared or changed while SESSION stays valid. Clearing it selectively in the browser is one way, or a backend that does not reissue the token.
- When a 403 does happen, every retry keeps failing, because nothing refreshes the token.

The point about repeated clicks is accurate: there is no `busy` state, so each click sends a DELETE. But it does no harm. The first DELETE returns 204 and later ones return 401, and both count as success.

Net effect: the error message misleads in a rare but reachable edge case. Sign-out does not fail silently and nothing is exposed to an attacker. Minor severity is right.

I'm marking this as refuted. The code matches what the finding describes, but the problem it predicts doesn't happen in this code.

1. **The data it describes doesn't exist.** The only query in `src/` is `ADMIN_SESSION_KEY` (`['admin','session']`). It's used at `AdminGate.tsx:16`, and both sign-out (`AdminArea.tsx:18`) and the 401 listener (`AdminGate.tsx:18`) set exactly that key. There is no other `['admin', …]` data to leave behind, so there's no defect today. The finding admits this itself.

2. **"Shown stale without a refetch" is wrong for this setup.** `src/app/queryClient.ts` changes only `retry` and `refetchOnWindowFocus`, so `staleTime` keeps TanStack's default of 0. When the session flag goes false, `AdminGate` swaps the children for `SignInForm`, which unmounts every child query observer. After the next sign-in the children mount again, and with `staleTime` 0 every query refetches on mount. If the data hasn't been garbage-collected yet (default `gcTime` is 5 min), it shows briefly while the refetch runs. That's normal show-cached-then-refresh behaviour, not stale data that never refreshes.

3. **No exposure to another user.** There's one admin role behind one password, so cached data staying in memory after sign-out doesn't show one user's data to another.

The helper the finding suggests (`removeQueries({queryKey:['admin']})`) is reasonable tidying for later slices. But a correctness finding needs a mechanism that actually fails here, and none does.

I read the code and the claimed problem can't happen today. The only TanStack Query cache entry in `src` is `ADMIN_SESSION_KEY`. A search for `queryKey`, `setQueryData` and `removeQueries` turned up only AdminGate.tsx:16, :18 and :34 plus AdminArea.tsx:18. There is no other `['admin', …]` data that could be left behind after sign-out or a 401, and the finding admits this ("No other admin queries exist yet"). So no real user or attacker can reproduce it.

The claim is also weak for future code:
1. When the session flag goes false, AdminGate unmounts its children. Queries using TanStack's default `staleTime` of 0 refetch when they mount again after the next sign-in.
2. There is only one admin, so cached data is not exposed to a different user.
3. Without a session the cache is never shown, because the gate renders SignInForm in place of the children.

At most this is a hardening idea for later slices, not a defect in the code under review.
